name: Vertical gaze pathway
summary: Vertical saccades are generated by the rostral interstitial nucleus of the MLF in the rostral midbrain, which drives the oculomotor and trochlear nuclei of both sides; up-gaze commands cross through the posterior commissure, which is why dorsal midbrain compression abolishes up-gaze first. The interstitial nucleus of Cajal holds vertical gaze position, and vestibular input from the anterior and posterior canals reaches the same nuclei through the MLF. Because the vestibular route bypasses the riMLF, a supranuclear vertical gaze palsy (progressive supranuclear palsy, Parinaud) can be overcome by the oculocephalic reflex.

origin.note: Frontal eye fields bilaterally and the superior colliculus; vestibular nuclei for reflex movements.

neuronChain.synapse: oculomotor nucleus (elevators and depressors) and trochlear nucleus, via the posterior commissure for up-gaze
superior rectus, inferior oblique (up); inferior rectus, superior oblique (down)

decussation.note: Up-gaze pathways cross in the posterior commissure; down-gaze projections are mainly ipsilateral.

waypoints.note: rostral interstitial nucleus of the MLF at the mesodiencephalic junction
posterior commissure for up-gaze; interstitial nucleus of Cajal for gaze holding
superior and inferior rectus, inferior oblique subnuclei

termination: Vertical extraocular muscles of both eyes through the oculomotor and trochlear nerves.

lesionEffectsByLevel.level: Posterior commissure / pretectum (pineal tumor, hydrocephalus, top of basilar)
lesionEffectsByLevel.effects: Up-gaze palsy with convergence-retraction nystagmus, lid retraction and light-near dissociation (Parinaud)
Loss of down-gaze (and up-gaze) saccades with somnolence
Slow then absent vertical saccades, down-gaze first, overcome by the oculocephalic reflex

lesionEffectsByLevel.level: Oculomotor and trochlear nuclei or nerves
lesionEffectsByLevel.effects: Nuclear or infranuclear palsy: not overcome by head movement, with ptosis or diplopia

pearls: Up-gaze palsy: think dorsal midbrain compression. Down-gaze palsy: think riMLF or PSP
A vertical gaze palsy overcome by the doll's-head maneuver is supranuclear
Elderly patients often have limited up-gaze normally; down-gaze limitation is never normal
